analysis.evidence: אַבְרָם is the subject. מִמִּצְרַיִם gives his point of departure, Egypt, and הַנֶּגְבָּה gives his destination, the Negev. The verb describes Abram’s journey up from Egypt.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ combines with the shortened Qal imperfect יַּעַל to form a third-person masculine singular wayyiqtol agreeing with אַבְרָם.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: אַבְרָם names the subject of וַיַּעַל, “went up.” Abram went up from Egypt toward the Negev, accompanied by his wife and Lot.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham
